task: Implement WorkflowPool singleton service with thread-safe compiled-graph pool, split WorkflowExecutor._init_workflow() into _compile_graph() + _inject_user_context(), background warmup watcher, and SubWorkflowNode pool acquire/release integration

key_reasoning.reason: Four components — WorkflowPool (new singleton service), WorkflowExecutor (core _init_workflow() split), SubWorkflowNode (pool acquire/release on create-path), main.py (startup hook + APScheduler warmup watcher) — across Service, Workflow, and API layers. Red-flag bumped from L to XL because WorkflowExecutor is a core shared utility: its refactor has blast-radius across every non-autonomous workflow execution in the system.

Two novel LangGraph-specific patterns with no local precedent: (1) splitting CompiledStateGraph build into a user-agnostic _compile_graph() phase and a user-dependent _inject_user_context() phase using NodeSlot placeholders, and (2) resetting CheckpointSaver state on a pooled CompiledStateGraph before reuse — no equivalent pattern exists in the codebase and must be derived from LangGraph internals. Additional risks: thread-safety correctness under concurrent pool acquire/release (no concurrency test infrastructure exists), circular import risk when importing WorkflowPool inside sub_workflow_node.py, and unresolved design question about how to make _compile_graph() callable by WorkflowPool without a full per-execution WorkflowExecutor instantiation.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L (4) to XL (5): WorkflowExecutor._init_workflow() is a core shared utility used by all non-autonomous workflow executions — structural refactor has wide blast radius across the system
